pairs.why: Both show smooth satin-gloss red paint with similar glassy panes, so surface gives little reason; A's edges are a touch softer.
B is smooth, soft clay-like matte plaster like the real sandcastle and lighthouse, while A's individual brick and shingle texture leans toward the too texture-y side.
B's tubes are softer lavender-grey satin like the real frame and its fabric is matte, while A's thin tubes read as shiny chrome.
A's brass is smooth with soft gradients like the real lamp and submarine, while B adds wax drips and hot specular streaks that look more lacquered and busy.
Both are the same chrome-tube and matte-fabric build; B adds slightly more stitch lines but nothing decisive.
A has a soft satin-plastic orange rim with restrained highlights like the real clock, while B has a glassier rim with a glow and stronger hot highlights.
Both show the same smooth lilac stone with faint marbling and no real cracks or chips, so surface gives no reason to choose.
A's soft lavender-grey tubes and matte fabric are closer to the real chair than B's bright chrome tube streaks.
